data.narrative:
Augury is a Series F robotics and manufacturing software company founded by Gal Shaul and Saar Yoskovitz that has raised $369M to date. The robotics and manufacturing sector includes one public comparable (277810.KQ) and eight private peers, though a sufficiently deep peer set meeting strict stage and valuation-tier criteria does not exist for a robust median-based approach.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable framework. Using total capital raised ($369M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.3x step-up multiplier typical of Series F advancement yields $480M. This method reflects the observable capital accumulation and progression trajectory but does not incorporate market multiples or comparable transaction data.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $408M to $552M, centered on $480M. This range assumes conventional Series F to later-stage expansion multiples hold and that $369M in total deployment correlates reasonably with current enterprise value. Key uncertainties include: (1) the absence of a statistically robust peer comparable set in the narrowly defined robotics and manufacturing sector at Augury's stage and scale, limiting cross-check validation; (2) the reliance on a single method rather than triangulated approaches; and (3) undocumented unit economics, revenue run-rate, or market conditions that may materially alter stage-appropriate multiples.
